atoms.canonical_statement: The study evaluated whether body mass index modifies cardiovascular and kidney outcomes associated with GLP-1 receptor agonists compared with DPP-4 inhibitors in type 2 diabetes.

The cohort included new users of GLP-1 receptor agonists or DPP-4 inhibitors with type 2 diabetes and excluded younger patients, type 1 diabetes, reduced-EF heart failure, bariatric surgery, prior SGLT2 inhibitor use, missing baseline HbA1c or BMI, short follow-up, and early treatment switching.

population.label: Eligible new users with type 2 diabetes
inclusion_criteria: First received a GLP-1 receptor agonist or DPP-4 inhibitor between 2011-12-15 and 2022-12-31
exclusion_criteria: Heart failure with ejection fraction under 40%
Treatment switching within the first 90 days

atoms.canonical_statement: Patients were stratified at a BMI threshold of 25 kg/m2 into BMI below 25 and BMI at least 25 groups.
The exposure group consisted of patients newly treated with GLP-1 receptor agonists.

atoms.canonical_statement: Major adverse cardiovascular events included cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, and hospitalization for heart failure.

outcome.definition: Composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, and hospitalization for heart failure

atoms.canonical_statement: The composite kidney outcome was an eGFR decline greater than 50% or progression to dialysis during follow-up.

outcome.definition: eGFR decline greater than 50% or progression to dialysis

atoms.canonical_statement: Secondary outcomes included all-cause death, infection-related admission, any-cause admission, major adverse lower-limb events, hypoglycemia, DKA or HHS, and newly diagnosed pancreatitis.

Propensity scores used the measured baseline covariates, greedy nearest-neighbor matching without replacement, and a caliper of 0.2 standard deviations of the logit; matching was performed separately by BMI stratum.
The primary matching analysis used single imputation with an expectation-maximization algorithm before matching, and standardized differences below 0.1 were treated as negligible imbalance.

Cardiovascular and all-cause deaths were analyzed with Cox models; nonfatal outcomes used Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards with death as a competing risk and robust standard errors for matched-pair clustering.

Continuous BMI effect modification was evaluated with restricted cubic splines using knots at the 10th, 50th, and 90th percentiles, with a four-knot specification at the 5th, 35th, 65th, and 95th percentiles as a robustness check.

Sensitivity analyses evaluated individual dulaglutide and liraglutide comparisons, prior SGLT2 inhibitor use, concomitant insulin, exclusion of thiazolidinedione exposure, exclusion of pancreatitis, IPTW using the ATT estimand, and multiple imputation with 10 datasets pooled by Rubin rules.
Cardiovascular MACE was not significantly different in the BMI below 25 stratum.

atoms.canonical_statement: Restricted cubic spline analyses indicated stronger cardiovascular associations for hospitalization for heart failure and MACE at higher BMI, while the composite kidney association persisted across BMI values and appeared stronger at lower BMI.

source_anchor.paragraph: eResults: restricted cubic spline interaction analysis

atoms.canonical_statement: The four-knot restricted cubic spline sensitivity analysis yielded a pattern similar to the three-knot analysis.

Dulaglutide and liraglutide analyzed separately generally showed associations consistent with the primary class-level analysis, although some comparisons lost statistical significance with smaller subgroup samples.

Among patients with BMI at least 25, the cardiovascular association for hospitalization for heart failure and MACE was less pronounced in patients with prior SGLT2 inhibitor exposure; interaction P values were below 0.05, but the source cautioned that the exposed subgroup was small.
The cardiovascular association appeared more evident among concomitant insulin users than nonusers, with reported interaction P values below 0.1.
Excluding thiazolidinedione-exposed patients preserved the direction of the main associations, although some estimates lost statistical significance after the sample was reduced.
Excluding patients with pancreatitis produced results consistent with the primary analysis.
Inverse probability of treatment weighting produced results consistent with the propensity-matched analysis.

Patients with complete and missing covariate data had substantial baseline differences, but multiple imputation with pooled multivariable estimates produced hazard ratios similar to the primary analysis.

source_anchor.paragraph: eResults: missing data and multiple imputation

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that cardiovascular associations with GLP-1 receptor agonists were BMI-dependent, whereas kidney-protective associations were present in both BMI groups.
The authors reported lower all-cause mortality, infection-related hospitalization, and all-cause hospitalization across BMI groups, while emphasizing increased hypoglycemia and DKA or HHS events.
The nonrandomized design leaves selection bias, residual confounding, reverse causality, and unmeasured factors such as lifestyle, socioeconomic status, and cardiac function.
Only baseline covariates were modeled, so time-varying confounding during follow-up was not accounted for, and excluding follow-up shorter than 90 days did not fully eliminate reverse causality.
The Chang Gung Research Database is a Taiwanese health-system database, which limits generalizability to other populations and care settings.
Potential diagnostic miscoding and medication adherence inferred from prescription records add measurement uncertainty.
The article reported no conflicts of interest.
